issues.fact: The fact sheet says nothing about how often the watch inspection happens. It only describes the 9 o'clock inspection at dinner.
issues.misreading: A solver could take 'every year' as a habit that bears on the master's routine or on how the watches were set, which is a duration the sheet does not give.

issues.quote: He worked on it for four years.
issues.fact: The sheet gives no duration for the repeater's construction.
issues.misreading: The four-year figure is an added duration. A solver could try to use it in the timeline or in the watch's history, which the sheet does not support.

issues.quote: He meant it to strike the first minute of the new century.
issues.fact: The sheet does not mention the repeater's intended striking time or any new-century date.
issues.misreading: This adds a target time for the watch. A solver could treat it as a clue about when the repeater was meant to sound or when it was set, which the sheet does not establish.

issues.quote: The low notes give the hours. Each quarter is a doubled note. The high notes give the minutes past the quarter.
issues.fact: The sheet has no information about how the repeater strikes or how its notes encode the time.
issues.misreading: This gives a striking convention that a solver could use to decode sounds as clock readings. The sheet supplies no such convention, so it could lead to a reading the facts do not support.

issues.quote: He was not a man who would be late for anything.
issues.fact: The sheet makes no claim about the master's punctuality or his whereabouts at any time.
issues.misreading: A solver could read this as a statement that the master kept exact time or would not have been delayed, which bears on how much weight to give his clock remarks or his whereabouts. The sheet does not say this.
